bibl.title: What Ancient Christian Manuscripts Reveal About Reading (and About Non-Reading).
bibl.seg: Christoph Markschies, What Ancient Christian Manuscripts Reveal About Reading (and About Non-Reading).

Anna Krauss, Jonas Leipziger & Friederike Schücking-Jungblut (edd.), Material Aspects of Reading in Ancient and Medieval Cultures. Materiality, Presence and Performance = Materiale Textkulturen. 26 (Berlin - Boston, 2020) pp. 197-216, figg.
bibl.note: Questions the characterisation of early Christianity as a "textual" or "reading community" by investigating the literacy of leading figures on the one hand and the handling of books in Christian communities on the other hand: the presence of (biblical) books cannot be taken as evidence for a widespread practice of careful reading, as they frequently served as magical objects or items of liturgical veneration.
